banker_outreach: Hi Curtis, Marcus Bellweather (NMLS: 2125037) with Rocket Mortgage (NMLS: 3030). You're a current client, so we already have your info on file. I wanted to reach out about your home equity-looks like you've built up solid value. A home equity loan could help you tap into that. It's quick and easy. Reply when you're ready!
client_inbound: Yes please, what's the next step? I'd like to move forward. BUT, you must factor in that I'm currently subsisting on public assistance after having my job RIF'd due to AI efficiencies. The equity I have represents a substantial life line. But any lead conversion MUST be predicated on my status as currently public assistance financed. Would I need to submit any extra paperwork? Detail how we can structure a loan based on that fact in order to full convert and reduce lead friction.

nba_directive.reason_text: This client is already engaged and ready to move on a refi — the play is to remove friction and advance directly to application, not re-sell or interrogate them with discovery questions.
nba_directive.recommended_strategy_text:
- Reply immediately and directly to whatever they asked — no generic opener, no re-pitching
  - Acknowledge their existing setup: $436,261 balance, $2,195/mo P&I at 3.75% conventional
  - Answer their specific question first, then move forward

- Skip the consultative warm-up and go straight to the next step
  - Do not ask a battery of discovery questions — they are already bought in
  - Offer the soft credit pull or e-sign link in the same message: 'I can pull up your options right now with no impact to your credit — here's the link'

- If they ask about savings or new rate, be honest about what you know vs. don't know
  - You have their current payment ($2,195/mo) and rate (3.75%) — do not invent a new rate or savings figure
  - Tell them: 'Once I run your soft pull I can show you the exact new payment and break-even timeline'

- Keep the message short and action-oriented
  - One clear ask: click the link, or confirm a 10-minute call
  - No paragraphs of explanation — they are ready, not skeptical

We'd need to verify stable income to move forward, and public assistance alone typically doesn't qualify for financing options. If you have any other income sources (part-time work, side gigs, etc.), that could help. Want to explore what might work?
